meta.description: Leave-one-out error of each fair price model, per kind of part, with the naive baseline.

sources.name: Amazon US listings via Bright Data
sources.licence: Bright Data customer terms. Amazon's own conditions of use do not permit automated collection; Bright Data collects public listing pages as a commercial service. Terms have not been read in full.

sources.name: Central Computers online store
sources.licence: No data licence. Public search pages are crawled where robots.txt allows it. Site terms of use have not been read.

sources.name: Blender Open Data benchmark snapshots
sources.licence: Published by Blender as public domain (CC0). Confirm on the site before relying on it.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; snapshots are regenerated daily

limitations: A fair price here means the price predicted from Blender rendering score alone. A part can cost more for reasons the benchmark does not measure, such as gaming performance, memory size or power draw.
Graphics cards are scored on different Blender backends (OptiX, HIP, oneAPI), which favours NVIDIA cards, so AMD and Intel cards look more expensive for their score.
The fit uses a few dozen parts. Gaps under the stated typical error are noise.

gpu.statement: No model clearly beats the same-price-per-point baseline on 20 parts, so the baseline sets the fair price. It is typically off by 33%, so read the gaps as rough.

cpu.statement: No model clearly beats the same-price-per-point baseline on 25 parts, so the baseline sets the fair price. It is typically off by 18%, so read the gaps as rough.

data.model: Straight line (log price on log score)
